name: Plan
what: The stage before the posting, at which the firm decides whether an opening is real, what it is, what it can pay and what it will cost. Realness is a matter of rules: a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) may be requested only for a contract need and never to build a cache [119](#cite:119), a person named in a proposal is a contingent hire who must be reported if unavailable [108](#cite:108) and may not be named without a reasonable basis to deliver them [203](#cite:203). Definition is a matter of three sources that have to be reconciled: the [labor category](#term:labor-category) the contract will pay for, which an audit found unvalidated for 1,219 of 1,287 employees and breached for 101 of 112 [99](#cite:99) [173](#cite:173); the structured, scored criteria the selection evidence supports [1](#cite:1) [7](#cite:7); and the customer's own standard, which the personal-services rule lets it apply to the result but not to the supervision of the hire [197](#cite:197). Price is arithmetic the firm can do in advance: market pay [110](#cite:110), loaded with fringe, [overhead](#term:overhead-rate), [G&A](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) and profit [206](#cite:206), against a category rate fixed at award [98](#cite:98) and a market rising 3 percent a year [103](#cite:103). Cost has three parts and only one shows on an invoice: the [acquisition spend](#term:cost-per-hire) (median \$1,200 per nonexecutive hire in 2025 [196](#cite:196)), the vacancy's cost (about a fifth of salary per replacement [180](#cite:180); [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) −.22 with customer satisfaction [181](#cite:181)) and the cash fronted between payroll and a 30-day payment [202](#cite:202). Partners can fill only half a [set-aside](#term:set-aside)'s services [198](#cite:198), with consent [199](#cite:199), and without a [no-poach](#term:no-poach-agreement) [187](#cite:187). Small firms run six [requisitions](#term:requisition) per recruiter [196](#cite:196), 87 percent of those hiring report few qualified applicants [71](#cite:71), and staffing decisions run on belief where the records that would correct them are not kept [204](#cite:204) [200](#cite:200).
decided_by: The customer and the contract decide whether the opening is funded, what category it bills and who approves the person [119](#cite:119) [99](#cite:99) [197](#cite:197); the market decides the price [110](#cite:110) [103](#cite:103); the law decides the records and the partner limits [200](#cite:200) [198](#cite:198); the firm decides the forecast, the scorecard, the budget, the cap and the owner [205](#cite:205) [196](#cite:196) (synthesis).

metrics.definition: Share of open requisitions with a named contract, category, funding line, decision authority and start date (synthesis from [119](#cite:119) [203](#cite:203)).
Open requisitions per person running them; median 6 at organisations under 100 employees [196](#cite:196).
Acquisition spend per hire as SHRM defines it; medians \$1,200 nonexecutive and \$10,625 executive in 2025 [196](#cite:196).
Unbilled hours, delivery at risk, cover strain and replacement cost per open requisition; the case-study median replacement cost is about 21 percent of salary [180](#cite:180) (synthesis).
Loaded market pay for the category against the contract ceiling [206](#cite:206) [98](#cite:98) [110](#cite:110) (synthesis).

name: Attract
what: The stage at which the opening reaches people who could fill it: the posting, the channels, the networks, the employer's image and the pool the law lets the firm draw on. What attracts applicants is [meta-analytically](#term:meta-analysis) settled at the category level: the job and the organisation, how recruiters behave, how the process feels, perceived fit and the expectation of being hired, with fit the strongest and recruiter demographics irrelevant [63](#cite:63) [62](#cite:62). What a posting draws is set by its title and its pay figure: within a title a 10 percent higher posted wage draws 7.7 percent more applicants [65](#cite:65). The best source by retention is [referral](#term:referral-hiring), 10 to 30 percent lower quit rates across nine firms [60](#cite:60), and the narrowest, because networks are segregated [81](#cite:81). Small firms report the thinnest pools: 87 percent of those hiring found few or no qualified applicants in September 2026 [71](#cite:71), relocation has fallen under two percent of job seekers [85](#cite:85), and workers price a hybrid option at 8 percent of pay [70](#cite:70). For [cleared](#term:security-clearance) work the pool is closed by the [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) rule [80](#cite:80).
decided_by: The market sets the pool and the going terms [71](#cite:71) [84](#cite:84); the firm decides the posting, the channels, the referral program and the work arrangement [65](#cite:65) [60](#cite:60) [70](#cite:70); the law decides the words, the listing duty and who may be excluded [78](#cite:78) [73](#cite:73) [49](#cite:49); the customer decides whether the work can be remote or uncleared (sweeps 4 and 7).

metrics.definition: Applicants meeting basic qualifications per opening, by source; the Uniform Guidelines' records by group are the base [31](#cite:31); small firms report few or none at 87% [71](#cite:71).
Share of hires from each source still employed at 90 days and one year; inside sources outperform outside ones [62](#cite:62).
Whether the posting shows a range; 59% of US postings did in May 2025 [75](#cite:75); required in thirteen states and DC [76](#cite:76).

name: Select
what: The stage at which the firm decides who to make an offer to, from screening applications through interviews and assessments to the scored decision. A century of research in one journal alone has treated this as applied psychology's "Supreme Problem" since 1917 [26](#cite:26). The 2022 re-estimation of selection validity puts [structured interviews](#term:structured-interview) first ([operational validity](#term:operational-validity) .42), then [job-knowledge tests](#term:job-knowledge-test) (.40), [empirically keyed biodata](#term:biodata) (.38), [work samples](#term:work-sample-test) (.33) and [cognitive ability](#term:cognitive-ability-test) (.31), with [unstructured interviews](#term:unstructured-interview) at .19 and years of experience at .07 [1](#cite:1). How the predictors are combined matters as much as which are used: [formula-based combination](#term:mechanical-combination) of the same information predicts job performance at r .44 against .28 for judgement [7](#cite:7), and managers who override a valid test make worse hires on average [10](#cite:10). Applicants, for their part, rate interviews and work samples most favourably and personality, [honesty tests](#term:integrity-test) and graphology least, and those perceptions predict whether they stay in the process and accept an offer [14](#cite:14).
decided_by: The firm decides the method and the decision rule; the law decides what may be asked and when [33](#cite:33) [34](#cite:34); where a customer must approve the candidate, the customer's criteria sit on top of the firm's (recorded in sweep 7; see h-B5 in the ledger).

metrics.definition: Days from requisition opening to accepted offer; SHRM reports a 2025 median of about 45 days for executive and nonexecutive roles [43](#cite:43). ISO/TS metric definitions exist for cost per hire, impact of hire and quality of hire [46](#cite:46).
Share of offers accepted; rises with faster post-interview offers in the one field study found, with no later performance or turnover penalty [15](#cite:15).
Share of candidates who leave a multi-stage process before a decision; correlates with perceptions of the organisation and the process, career commitment and relocation needs [16](#cite:16).

Selection rate of each race, sex or ethnic group divided by the highest group's rate; below four-fifths is generally regarded as evidence of adverse impact, qualified by statistical and practical significance [31](#cite:31).

name: Offer
what: The stage at which the firm names a number and the candidate decides. For a customer-governed firm the number has a ceiling the firm did not set: the labor-category rate contains wages, [indirect costs](#term:overhead-rate) and profit [98](#cite:98) and pays only for labor that meets the category's qualifications [99](#cite:99), so the affordable salary is the residue of a rate fixed at award while market wages rise about 3 percent a year [103](#cite:103). What the candidate compares is wider than the salary: benefits are 30 percent of compensation cost [104](#cite:104), working conditions are compensation in their own right [94](#cite:94), and workers price a work-from-home option at about 8 percent of wages and schedule predictability at about 20 percent [115](#cite:115). The offer process itself is now regulated: ranges in postings [76](#cite:76), no questions about prior pay in about twenty states [106](#cite:106), equal pay for [substantially equal work](#term:equal-pay-act) with no cure by cutting [112](#cite:112), and bonuses on cost-type contracts only under a plan that predates the work [100](#cite:100). Speed is the one offer-stage [lever](#term:lever-record) with field evidence [15](#cite:15), and every market-rate offer becomes the incumbents' comparison point [92](#cite:92) [93](#cite:93).
decided_by: The contract sets the rate ceiling and the wage floor [98](#cite:98) [101](#cite:101); the market sets the going pay [103](#cite:103) [110](#cite:110); the law sets what may be asked and how differences are justified [106](#cite:106) [112](#cite:112); the firm sets the range, the package statement and the process [15](#cite:15) [95](#cite:95); the candidate decides, with the current employer's counteroffer in hand [113](#cite:113).

metrics.definition: Offers accepted over offers extended; rises with faster offers in the one field study [15](#cite:15).
The affordable range midpoint over the OEWS metro median for the SOC code [110](#cite:110) (synthesis).
New-hire pay over incumbent pay in substantially equal jobs; external hires ran about 18% above internal promotees in the one firm measured [93](#cite:93).

name: Clear and start
what: The stage between an accepted offer and a productive first day, which for a customer-governed firm runs on other people's clocks. A [clearance](#term:security-clearance) can be requested only for an employee whose access a classified contract requires, never to build a bench, and only by a firm whose [facility clearance](#term:facility-clearance) someone else [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) [119](#cite:119) [120](#cite:120). An investigation requested before employment needs a written commitment and a start within 45 days of the grant [119](#cite:119); [DCSA](#term:dcsa)'s industry cases averaged 197 days [end to end](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) for a [Secret](#term:secret) and 243 for a [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) in FY2026 Q3 [126](#cite:126) [125](#cite:125), against targets of 40 and 75 [54](#cite:54) and a median [time to fill](#term:time-to-fill) of about 45 [43](#cite:43), and the published figures understated the real ones for five years [56](#cite:56). [Eligibility is not access](#term:eligibility-versus-access): the credential needs a sponsor, a fingerprint check and a submitted investigation [138](#cite:138) [137](#cite:137), a transferred clearance a [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) decision the rule puts at five business days and agencies do not track [122](#cite:122) [145](#cite:145), and a cyber role its foundational certificate on day one [139](#cite:139). The wait itself is a cost: among 157,154 accepted offers at one employer, each additional week between acceptance and start raised the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) by 22 percent [144](#cite:144), and payroll in the interval is the firm's [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate), not the customer's [98](#cite:98) [148](#cite:148). The start carries statutory clocks of its own: [Section 2 of Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) within three business days [130](#cite:130), [E-Verify](#term:e-verify) within three business days of hire [128](#cite:128), the [FCRA notices](#term:fair-credit-reporting-act) before any adverse decision [136](#cite:136), and the export assessment for a controlled position, apart from the I-9 [131](#cite:131) [132](#cite:132).
decided_by: The government decides eligibility and its timing [119](#cite:119) [126](#cite:126); the customer sponsors the credential, the account and the read-in [138](#cite:138) [119](#cite:119); the law fixes the start-date checks [128](#cite:128) [130](#cite:130) [136](#cite:136); the firm controls the request, the interval it does not have to wait, the communication and the work available in it [144](#cite:144) [148](#cite:148); the candidate decides whether to keep waiting [144](#cite:144).

metrics.definition: Days from acceptance to the first productive day; each week added 22 percent to the odds of a no-show in the one field study [144](#cite:144).
Days from initiation to adjudication for an industry case; DCSA reports initiation, investigation and adjudication separately, now as averages of all cases [126](#cite:126).
Days from the start date to the first hour chargeable to the contract; no public benchmark was found (synthesis).
Share of sponsored hires granted temporary eligibility and the days to that decision; no public figure exists [127](#cite:127).

name: Onboard
what: The first ninety days, in which the hire becomes someone who knows the role, can do the tasks and is accepted by the people. The current [meta-analysis](#term:meta-analysis) of 183 [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment) samples puts the firm's structured tactics at r .24 to .40 with those three kinds of adjustment and the [social tactics](#term:socialization-tactics), experienced insiders as guides and affirmation of what the hire brings, at .29 to .47, the strongest of any [152](#cite:152); social acceptance then carries performance (.35), [intentions to leave](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) (−.27) and leaving (−.12) [152](#cite:152). At one firm with no [orientation](#term:onboarding) program a quarter of newcomers left within a year and insider role models roughly halved the odds [155](#cite:155); across fourteen weekly surveys of new hires, supervisor and coworker support fell week by week, what the newcomer got early predicted integration and commitment at ninety days, and an undermining supervisor tripled the hazard of leaving [156](#cite:156). Output rose 53 percent over the first year where it could be counted, far faster than pay [157](#cite:157), while the labor-category rate assumed the finished worker from the first hour [98](#cite:98) and pays only for people who meet the category [99](#cite:99), a rule an audit found enforced to the tune of about \$35 million in potential improper payments [173](#cite:173).
decided_by: The firm decides the program, the insider and the supervisor's attention [152](#cite:152) [156](#cite:156); the contract decides what the hire may be billed as [99](#cite:99); the customer decides whether a junior is accepted in the slot [173](#cite:173) (and, where it approves by name, sweep 7); the newcomer's own proactivity decides a share the firm cannot [152](#cite:152).

metrics.definition: Role clarity, task mastery and social acceptance at ninety days, the three adjustment indicators of the meta-analytic model [152](#cite:152) [153](#cite:153); early support predicts them [156](#cite:156).
Share of hires leaving voluntarily within twelve months; 24.8 percent at one firm with no orientation program [155](#cite:155).
Days to the output the labor category assumes; output rose 53 percent over the first year where it is counted, and no public benchmark exists for technical staff [157](#cite:157) (synthesis).

name: Develop
what: The stage at which the firm spends money and senior time making a hire worth more, knowing the result is portable. The economics explain why firms pay for [general skills](#term:general-human-capital) at all: the training firm knows what the worker can do better than the market does [161](#cite:161), and training raises output about twice as much as it raises pay, so the firm keeps the difference while the person stays [159](#cite:159). Learning from knowledgeable coworkers is itself four to nine percent of what a job pays [158](#cite:158), which is the price of the [mentoring](#term:mentoring) a small firm has to find in its seniors' billable hours [99](#cite:99) [148](#cite:148). What transfers from training to the job depends on realistic practice, a supervisor who expects the skill used, and an early chance to use it [162](#cite:162); what the protégé gains from mentoring is small on the measurable outcomes [164](#cite:164) [165](#cite:165). The return arrives partly through who the offer of training attracts (80 percent of a tuition program's retention effect) [160](#cite:160), and the instruments once used to hold it are narrowing: nearly a tenth of workers had a [repayment agreement](#term:training-repayment-agreement) in 2020 [166](#cite:166), California bars most such terms for contracts after January 1, 2026 [167](#cite:167), Colorado limits them to distinct training at cost declining over two years [168](#cite:168), and the federal [noncompete](#term:noncompete-agreement) rule is gone [169](#cite:169). The cost rules allow job-related training in the rates and forbid it for non-employees [175](#cite:175); the tax code excludes \$5,250 a year of [educational assistance](#term:section-127-plan) under a written plan [174](#cite:174); the FLSA makes most training paid time for non-exempt staff [170](#cite:170). [Apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) is the registered form: about 940,000 participants, computer occupations third, with the registration burden and the cost that smaller employers name [172](#cite:172) and completers' career gains of \$240,037 [171](#cite:171).
decided_by: The firm decides what to fund and who teaches [175](#cite:175) [158](#cite:158); the law decides what it may hold the worker to [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168) [169](#cite:169) and what it must pay for [170](#cite:170); the contract decides what the trained person may be billed as [99](#cite:99); the market decides what the new skill is worth elsewhere [89](#cite:89) [161](#cite:161).

metrics.definition: Whether the trained skill is used on the job within weeks; predicted by supervisor support (ρ .31), climate (.37) and opportunity to perform [162](#cite:162).
Cohort training cost and mentoring hours against billed hours by category and retention at 12 and 24 months (synthesis); the economics give the terms [159](#cite:159) [157](#cite:157).
Share still employed 12 and 24 months after a certification or clearance; no public benchmark found; the cleared market's switching rate is the comparison [89](#cite:89) (synthesis).

name: Retain
what: The stage at which the firm keeps the people it has [cleared](#term:security-clearance), trained and placed, against a market that prices what it taught them. The turnover evidence is a ranked list: wanting to leave (ρ .56) and looking (.40), then commitment, fit and satisfaction near −.3, [embeddedness](#term:job-embeddedness) (−.26), the supervisor (−.24) and the alternatives the person sees (.23), with pay at −.17 and hours of workload at −.10 while stress, role conflict and work–life conflict run .15 to .21 [178](#cite:178). Pay moves people through comparison: quits at a large employer responded to peers' raises more than to the market and hardly at all when raises were similar [182](#cite:182), and each market-rate hire resets the comparison [93](#cite:93) [92](#cite:92). At the unit level, turnover lowers customer satisfaction and productivity at about −.22 and profit margin at −.15, and the practices that hold a unit together are [firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) (−.40), internal mobility (−.25) and selective hiring (−.24), with staffing levels, straight pay and [general training](#term:general-human-capital) not significant [181](#cite:181). The case-study median cost of a replacement is about a fifth of salary [180](#cite:180), against practitioner multiples that name no study [195](#cite:195). The arrangements an onsite cleared job cannot offer are worth 8 to 20 percent of pay [115](#cite:115), a long commute adds ten points to the chance of moving [194](#cite:194), and a visible contract end is a [withdrawal cognition](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) with no successor right behind it [186](#cite:186). The firm may not agree with a [prime](#term:prime-contractor) not to hire each other's people [187](#cite:187); what holds people is the job [178](#cite:178) [181](#cite:181).
decided_by: The person decides, on comparisons the firm partly controls [182](#cite:182) [178](#cite:178); the customer decides the site, the hours and the contract's end [115](#cite:115) [186](#cite:186); the law decides what the firm may hold the person to [187](#cite:187) [169](#cite:169) [167](#cite:167); the firm decides the pay review, the ladder, the manager and the links [181](#cite:181) [178](#cite:178).

metrics.definition: Voluntary separations over average headcount per year; economy-wide quits ran 1.9 percent a month in August 2026 [57](#cite:57); 24.8 percent of newcomers in a year at one firm without onboarding [155](#cite:155).
The two strongest leading indicators, at ρ .56 and .40 with actual leaving [178](#cite:178); heard in check-ins or measured by survey.
Separation, replacement, training and lost productivity per departure; case-study median about 21 percent of salary, more for specialists in thin markets [180](#cite:180) [193](#cite:193).

name: Hand over
what: The stage at which a person leaves, moves or is replaced, and the contract and the security rules notice. A named key person cannot be diverted without the contracting officer's written consent and, in the clause carried here, 30 days' notice with a substitute whose skills, experience and credentials meet or exceed the requirement [188](#cite:188); a proposed key person who becomes unavailable before award must be reported to the agency [108](#cite:108); a [cleared](#term:security-clearance) employee's termination is reported and adverse information is reported even after the person has gone [189](#cite:189); a firm of 100 or more owes 60 days' notice before a site-level layoff [191](#cite:191); no [right of first refusal](#term:nondisplacement) with a [successor contractor](#term:successor-contractor) survives the nondisplacement order's revocation [186](#cite:186). The cost of the departure is largest where the knowledge is concentrated: when a specialist is suddenly gone the firm pays the remaining specialists more and the people around them are worth less, most of all in thin markets [193](#cite:193), and [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) shows in customer satisfaction and productivity at about −.22 [181](#cite:181). [Firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) is the practice most tied to keeping a unit together (−.40) [181](#cite:181); internal mobility keeps people (−.25) and opens a vacancy with the full clock behind it [181](#cite:181) [126](#cite:126); the succession metrics a firm should be able to report are in the human-capital standard [46](#cite:46).
decided_by: The contract decides the notice and the substitute [188](#cite:188); the security rules decide the reports [189](#cite:189); the law decides the layoff notice [191](#cite:191); the firm decides whether a second holder and a successor exist before the day comes [181](#cite:181) [46](#cite:46); the person decides the day (synthesis).

metrics.definition: Contract tasks and customer relationships held by one person with no named successor; the ISO human-capital standard names succession metrics [46](#cite:46) (synthesis).

Days from notice to an approved substitute; the clause carried requires 30 days' notice and an equal-or-better substitute [188](#cite:188); the backfill clock behind it is the clearance clock where one is needed [126](#cite:126).
Separations over headcount at the contract or team level; correlates about −.22 with customer satisfaction and production efficiency [181](#cite:181).
